content:
Aisha: Heads up — customer NovaForms (enterprise account) reported their summary endpoint is returning invented partners, dates, and false revenue numbers since yesterday's canary swap. They flagged this as a high-severity QA regression.
Aisha: Example from their ticket: prompt -> 'Summarize NovaForms partnership history with Acme and key milestones.'
Aisha: ```
REQUEST: POST /v1/generate model=redwood-v2-fastpath variant=fp-int8
{
  "input": "Summarize NovaForms partnership history with Acme and key milestones."
}
RESPONSE: 200
{
  "output": "NovaForms partnered with Acme in 2018, acquired MicroLedger in 2020, and reported a $120M ARR in 2021."
}
request_id: req_0x9f4b2c
```
Aisha: All three claims are false per customer — they never partnered with Acme, no acquisition, and ARR numbers completely fabricated. They say this worked as expected on v2.1 yesterday and regressed after the canary we rolled at ~2199980000.
Marek: Can you paste the exact canary id and route the customer hit? Any model variant/quant config in the request?
Aisha: Canary: fastpath-routes v1.8 (rolled 2199981200). Customer hit model redwood-v2-fastpath fp-int8 by default. No explicit quant param in their call.
Sam: Pulled traces for req_0x9f4b2c — routed through us-east-1 -> pool-dedicated-3 -> fp-int8 handler. Latency looked normal (p95 ~120ms). No downstream errors.
Tori: Customer is on a paid enterprise plan with a 99.9% SLA. Marking as P1 for CS. We should offer a temporary routing override to the stable model and credits if we can't resolve quickly. @Marek can you triage?
Marek: On it. Initial hypothesis: fp-int8 kernel path + fastpath routing changed tokenization/segmentation or prompt pre-processing in the canary. That can cause hallucination patterns if prefix handling changed. Also possible that fallback to a smaller context model occurred for some shards.
Marek: Quick repro steps request: Aisha, can you share a minimal curl reproducer and one or two more examples (different prompts) where the customer sees fabricated facts? Also include the customer account ID and region.
Aisha: Repro steps pasted to ticket and below.
Aisha: ```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-v2-fastpath","input":"Summarize NovaForms partnership history with Acme and key milestones."}'
```
Aisha: Additional example where model invents a board member and date: prompt 'List NovaForms leadership changes since 2017.' -> response names someone who never worked there and a bogus 2019 "reorg." request_id: req_0x9f4b2d
Sam: I checked routing logs for 2199981200-2199983600 window. There were two quick autoscaling events and one transparent fallback to fp-compat-legacy on pool-dedicated-3 for ~7s (due to a hot GPU transient). Could the fallback explain the different behavior?
Marek: Possibly. fp-compat-legacy runs slightly different tokenization/decoder heuristics; mixing outputs across variants could produce confident but incorrect statements. We need to confirm whether the customer request experienced a split K/V cache or a cross-variant reroute mid-request.
deploy-bot: fastpath-routes v1.8 deployed at 2199981200 by ci/canary pipeline — changes include: prefix-normalization tweak and new quant kernel fp-int8-v2.
Marek: That prefix-normalization tweak is exactly the kind of change that can alter interpretation of short prompts (we shortened some whitespace trimming). Also new fp-int8-v2 kernel has different rounding behavior — putting this as top suspect.
Tori: For mitigation, can we route NovaForms to redwood-v2-stable (no int8) immediately? They want an immediate fix.
Sam: Added routing override for account NovaForms -> redwood-v2-stable at 2199990500. Monitoring now.
Aisha: Customer confirmed after override that outputs are back to expected for the two repro prompts. They sent green screenshots. They're still worried about trust.
Marek: Good signal. Next steps: 1) Reproduce locally with fp-int8-v2 + prefix-normalization enabled 2) Run a unit eval on the customer's prompt set against fp-int8-v2 vs stable 3) If we reproduce, rollback fp-int8-v2 or patch prefix handling. I'll take 1+2.
Aisha: I opened a formal CS escalation and linked the customer's logs and request_ids. Ticket #CS-11988. I offered a temporary credit and the routing override. Customer accepted the override and wants a postmortem.
Marek: Starting a bisect job now — will test the prefix-normalization toggle and kernel variant. Will report back with repro command and minimal diff.
Sam: Oncall assigned: Sam -> escalation channel set up. If bisect shows kernel culprit, we should pause further fastpath canaries.
Tori: Thanks team. @Aisha keep the customer updated and schedule a 1:1 postmortem with them once we have root cause. :thumbsup:
Aisha: Will do. I'll add the customer-confirmed screenshots to CS-11988 and update SLA credits.
Marek: Quick note for the run: include examples that previously worked on v2.1 to show regression delta. Also capture tokenization offsets for the repro requests (to see where prefix normalization shifted token boundaries).
Aisha: Copy that — adding tokenization artifacts to the ticket.
Sam: I'll keep an eye on related alerts. If we see more accounts with similar reports, we'll escalate faster.
Tori: Filing an action item: hold new fastpath canaries until a fix is in place or we have a mitigation plan.
Aisha: Closing loop for now — customer back on stable, mitigation applied, escalation created. Will post updates in CS-11988.
Marek: I'll update here when bisect completes.
Aisha: Thanks all. :pray:
